walkthroughs.body_html:
Database Concepts — a core area of GCSE Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Database Concepts brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Database Concepts.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which technique involves breaking a problem into smaller sub-problems?
options: Abstraction
Decomposition
Iteration
Encapsulation

mcqs.q: What is the purpose of a trace table?
options: To compile code
To track variable values during execution
To draw a flowchart
To store program output

mcqs.q: What does inheritance allow a subclass to do?
options: Reuse and extend the attributes and methods of its superclass.
Copy code from any unrelated class.
Replace the superclass entirely.
Because UDP is always faster than TCP.

mcqs.q: Why is UDP used for live video streaming despite being unreliable?
options: Because UDP is always faster than TCP.
Because TCP cannot handle video data.
Copy code from any unrelated class.
Lower overhead and latency - retransmitting late packets would harm real-time quality.

mcqs.q: What is the key difference between a compiler and an interpreter?
options: A compiler translates the whole program first; an interpreter executes line by line.
They produce different programming languages.
Copy code from any unrelated class.
A compiler is a person, an interpreter is software.
